- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) or mixed with sharp drops, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% to account for mean reversion.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85% of recent high), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap forecast decline at 10% below peak or adjust to 80% of peak.  
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; apply a 3–7 day lag correction: reduce forecast by 1–3% per day until sentiment stabilizes.  
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates in bearish sentiment cycles; add 1–3% bias upward to compensate for mean reversion toward prior 18-day average.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.33/1.00 alternation, model tends to oscillate; smooth forecast by averaging 3–5 prior values or apply exponential decay weighting.
